classification.difficultyReason: Represent the boat, cliff base and cliff top as a right triangle, interpret the elevation angle and identify height and horizontal distance as opposite and adjacent. One routine tangent calculation completes the model.

content.prompt: The angle of elevation of the top of a vertical cliff is observed to be $41^{\circ}$ from a boat $450\text{ m}$ from the base of the cliff. What is the height of the cliff, correct to the nearest metre?

answer.worked:
Let the height of the cliff be $h$ metres. Relative to the $41^{\circ}$ angle, the height is opposite and the horizontal distance is adjacent, so use tangent.
$$\begin{align*}\tan41^{\circ}&=\frac{h}{450}\\h&=450\tan41^{\circ}\\h&\approx391\text{ m}\end{align*}$$
The cliff is $391\text{ m}$ high, correct to the nearest metre.
